_note: Leads from scripts/local_fixes.py checked against public records. 'verified' means a documented change at that corner whose timing matches the drop; the crash numbers are from local_fix_candidates.csv. Still to do before the demo: hand-check imagery and confirm the NW 69th Ter turn-lane detail with FDOT project documents.

findings.change: FDOT Newberry Road project: extended turn lanes on SR 26 (Newberry Rd), widened the I-75 Exit 387 ramps, new traffic signals and street lighting. Construction September 2019 to spring 2020. Satellite imagery shows dual eastbound left-turn lanes at NW 69th Ter.
findings.effect: about 45% fewer crashes in 2021-2025 than 2015-2019 after adjusting for the citywide drop (similar-size corners: 0.52x relative change, p = 2e-07)
findings.caveats: The project's stated aim was congestion, not safety. The I-75 ramp work nearby could also change how crashes are named or located. Regression to the mean is limited by 5 steady years before (35-43 a year).

findings.intersection_id: W UNIVERSITY AVE corridor (NW 18th St, NW 19th St, NW 22nd St, NW 12th St, SW 2nd Ave, SW 23rd St)
findings.change: FDOT/UF pedestrian safety package in 2021: 25 mph limit from just east of NW 21st Terrace to NW 13th St (announced May 2021), crosswalk enhancements, signal retiming, temporary speed tables; new signals at NW 16th and NW 19th St from August 2021; one-way pattern at NW 17th/18th St; raised crosswalks and lighting from 2023.
findings.effect: The whole corridor fell relative to the city: the 25 mph section 27% fewer crashes (2022-25 vs 2015-19), but the stretch west of it (NW 22nd-40th St), which got no speed reduction, fell 34%. The 25 mph section was already declining in 2015-2019, and the NW 18th/19th St drops start in 2017-2018, before the package.
findings.caveats: Do not present as a proven fix. UF's remote classes in 2020-21 and other corridor changes are not controlled for.
